expectation: Membrane/surface stain on antigen-presenting cells (dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells) as scattered stellate single cells in the lamina propria, plus some in lymphoid aggregates. Gut epithelium can express HLA-DR dimly. Common to moderate, partly on CD163 cells.
observed: A: bright yellow specks scattered through villus cores and crypt regions, plus diffuse epithelial signal. B/C: dim epithelial lining haze with a few bright isolated cells. D: one bright elongated cell with processes. E: many bright branched, stellate cells, a subset overlapping CD163 and many CD163-negative.
why: Bright dendritic-shaped cells are scattered in the lamina propria and, in row E, sit partly on CD163 cells, as the marker graph relation predicts.
notes: Row E shows distinct bright stellate HLADRA cells, a subset co-localising with CD163, and A shows discrete bright cells in the stroma. Dim epithelial haze in B and C is likely background or minor epithelial signal, not the verdict.
